title: Helping a New Food Feel Less Scary | Parenting Rewind
description:
A new food lands on the plate and is rejected on sight. A practical pause-and-rewind response for parents.

General parenting education; every child and family is different.
audience_intent: Adults and parents; not directed to children
education_scope: General parenting education only; not personalised therapy, diagnosis, or medical advice.

narration.transcript: A new food lands on the plate and is rejected on sight. Requiring a big bite can make exploration feel unsafe. Before reacting, pause for one breath so the next words can be short, clear, and useful. Offer a tiny portion beside familiar food and allow steps such as touching, smelling, or tasting without pressure. Repeated low-pressure exposure is practice, not a test; one refusal does not predict the future.

source.title: 10 Tips for Parents of Picky Eaters

claim_limits: The suggested wording is an example, not a guarantee.
Families should adapt expectations to age, development, safety and individual needs.
